title: Input & Output
summary: Reading input with input(), and formatting output with print() and f-strings.

checkpoints.title: print() and input()
checkpoints.content: `print()` writes text to the screen — it can take multiple values separated by commas, and adds a space between them automatically. `input("prompt")` shows a prompt and waits for the user to type something, always returning it as a string, even if they typed digits.
checkpoints.explanation: input() always returns a string — if you need a number, you have to convert it yourself with int() or float().

hints.H0: print("a", "b") automatically puts a space between a and b.
hints.H1: Whatever the user types into input() comes back as text, never a number.
hints.H2: To do math with input, wrap it in int(...) or float(...) first.

checkpoints.title: Format a greeting
checkpoints.explanation: An f-string with `{name}` inserted directly, then the literal punctuation around it.

hints.H0: You'll need an f-string to insert the name into the sentence.
hints.H1: Remember the `f` prefix before the opening quote.

checkpoints.title: Predict input()'s type
checkpoints.content: A user runs `value = input("Enter a number: ")` and types `42`. What is `type(value)`?

options.explanation: input() always returns a string, regardless of what the user typed.
input() never converts to a number automatically — you'd need int(value) for that.

options.text: It raises an error since 42 isn't quoted.
options.explanation: The user typed 42 at a prompt, not in code — input() just captures it as text, no quoting needed.

checkpoints.explanation: input() always hands back a string — converting to a number is something you do afterward, explicitly.

hints.H0: This is true no matter what the user types, even pure digits.
hints.H1: Converting to a number is a separate, manual step.

checkpoints.title: Convert input to a number
checkpoints.content: Given `raw = input("Age: ")`, write an expression that converts it to an integer.
checkpoints.explanation: Wrapping the string in int(...) parses it as a whole number.

hints.H0: You need the built-in that converts text digits into a number.
hints.H1: Wrap the variable, don't reassign input() again.
